items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: He told me also he tried to get Louie, and Louie said, oh, it's not any vocal, I want something I can kind of jive and he wouldn't fool with it.

ctx.x: He told me also he tried to get Louie, and Louie said, oh, it's not any vocal, I want something I can kind of jive and he wouldn't fool with it.

They considered it as kind of a corny number, which it was, because it was just a saxophone exercise, but they couldn't anticipate how big it would be, and so naturally--I heard Count Basie play it in 1938, the same year that it was so very popular, thirty eight or thirty nine, Earl Warren in the reed section just tripped on out and they made it likeable; but the rock version you made, that Plas was marvelous.
